alt: Raymond sammenligner den lange søgebakke med et fanebladskartotek ved havnen. Docker tager tid, og Gitmejsen følger den samme klokkemærkede prøve.
prompt: ONE standalone complete 1536×1024 landscape (3:2), richly detailed warm painted LUP storybook scene with gouache and softly brushed oil on textured paper. Use exact canonical mascot likenesses from attached local references, exactly THREE main characters with natural plausible limbs and readable faces. Concrete learning activity rather than a text chart. No readable text, headings, digits, fake code, watermark, external logo, borders or multiple panels. Teach index lookup versus sequential scanning and measured performance on same fixed query. On a sunlit harbor sorting archive workbench, a broad long shallow wooden sequential-scan tray to left contains a neat long run of many indistinct cream record-card backs, curved through the bench depth, no marks on these backs. At right sits a compact upright alphabetic-style index rack with a FEW clearly distinguished colored tabs, but no writing or letters on tabs. Both search routes converge onto a single large target order card at center front on stand, showing ONE very distinctive plain brass BELL stamp. Exactly one target card exists, not separate result cards for two searches. A long amber thread loops along the sequential tray’s many cards then reaches the shared target; a short straight cool teal thread comes from one tab of the index rack directly to that SAME target card, simple and visible, not tangled. Raymond from first reference is canonical blue elephant professor with round bronze glasses, warm eyes, curled trunk, cream knit cardigan and blue shirt, brown trousers, stands left demonstrating long and short routes with natural pointer and closed little notebook. Docker from second ref, huge slate-gray humpback whale with cream grooved throat, bumpy face, navy cable-knit sweater and mustard beanie, rises beside the water at right, holding a small legible analog STOPWATCH with a plain dial and one hand but NO digits in his natural flipper, measuring repeated trials calmly. Gitmejsen from third ref, tiny actual crested tit with black speckled pale crest, black cheek arcs and bib, tan feathers, cobalt wool scarf, perches center on twig platform behind target and holds a little wooden test medallion securely under her natural talon; medallion bears identical small bell icon to show the same test is kept. View across tactile papers, warm wood and brass with pastel blue water, softly distant cargo masts. Keep all three mascots and fixed bell card clear, paths easy to follow, do not paint graphs, labels, timing values, UI or extra target results.
refinementPrompt: Localized anatomy fix for this exact landscape. Preserve ALL current scene and layout, the excellent shared bell card with two route cords, stopwatch, three character faces, exact cream/brown crested tit with blue scarf, the archive trays and painted style. Remove ONLY the extra human-looking hand and forearm floating immediately to the RIGHT of the crested tit’s face and above the small round bell medallion. This bird has two natural wings folded to body and two natural gray feet already clearly gripping its twig, all those remain. The SMALL bell medallion must instead hang from a simple short twine loop fastened around the twig, not from any hand. The bird never holds any object using a hand. Keep the natural beak, face and crest exactly as reference. Return the same full landscape with correct natural bird anatomy.
